items.title: Joint GP and community pharmacy conference to return for 2027 in London
items.summary: GPs and community pharmacy professionals are invited to a free-to-attend conference in London next June which aims to bring the two groups together to collaborate as the Government aims to shift care out of hospital.

items.title: Community Pharmacy and General Practice Conference returns in 2027
items.summary: Primary care nursing professionals will have the opportunity to explore how closer working between general practice and community pharmacy can improve patient care at the second annual Community Pharmacy and General Practice Conference, which moves to London in 2027.

items.title: Birmingham and Solihull Integrated Medicines Optimisation Committee (IMOC) minutes: new minutes listed: IMOC Minutes 2026 09 (September 2026)
items.summary: The list at this address now includes "IMOC Minutes 2026 09 (September 2026)", which was not in the list stored on 2026-10-16. It has not been read by a person; open it to see what it says.

items.title: What will the arrival of thousands of new pharmacist prescribers mean for general practice?
items.summary: This autumn sees the first cohort of pharmacists to graduate with prescribing powers. It means thousands more independent prescribers working in the community. Emma Wilkinson looks at the plans for NHS services and the safeguards being put in place. What has changed?

items.title: Dispensing GP practices should deliver pharmacy services in rural areas, report says
items.summary: Dispensing GP practices should be commissioned to deliver pharmacy services in rural areas, a new report has recommended.

items.title: Pharmacy First-issued medicines increase by nearly a third
items.summary: Last year saw a substantial jump in the number of medicines issued through Pharmacy First clinical consultations, figures show.

items.title: HRT patches out of stock until end of November
items.summary: A brand of transdermal hormone replacement therapy (HRT) patch is out of stock, the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) has announced.

items.title: ASA clamps down on rule-breaking pharmacy weight-loss medicine adverts
items.summary: The Advertising Standards Agency (ASA) has clamped down for the first time on online promotion of oral weight loss drugs. It found two online pharmacies had broken the rules by promoting unlicenced medicines and prescription-only medicines to the public in adverts for oral GLP-1 treatments.

items.title: Information for nurse prescribers on Levemir discontinuation issued
items.summary: A National Patient Safety Alert has been issued over the discontinuation of the diabetes drug Levemir in December. Stocks of Levemir (insulin detemir) FlexPen pre-filled pens and Penfill cartridges are expected to be exhausted by the end of the year.
